title: Propensity-score matching for the effect in the treated (ATT)
summary: 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on the logit of the propensity score with a caliper, balance diagnostics, and a pair-clustered standard error.

sizing._why: Matching discards unmatched patients and targets the treated; sizing depends on the ratio of controls to treated and on the overlap, which no catalog form takes. Simulation.

pinned_defaults: Both: 1:1 nearest neighbour without replacement; distance = the LOGIT of a logistic propensity score (MatchIt link = 'linear.logit'); caliper 0.2 SD of that distance over the whole sample; treated matched from the largest distance down (m.order = 'largest'); estimand ATT. MatchIt's own defaults differ: no caliper, and the score itself as the distance.
Both: the SE clusters on the matched pair (sandwich::vcovCL by subclass, HC1; statsmodels' cluster covariance with the same small-sample factor).

Python: no package documents MatchIt-compatible defaults, so the greedy algorithm is written out, ties going to the control first in the data. It reproduces MatchIt's matched set exactly on this fixture.
_att_not_ate: Matching keeps every treated patient it can and finds each a control, so it estimates the effect in the TREATED. Here the effect grows with severity and the treated are sicker: ATT 2.68, ATE 2.00. Dropping treated patients outside the caliper moves the target towards the ATE; report how many were dropped (18 of 751 here).
